📝 War is more profitable 📝 than covering budget deficits Amid discussions in recent weeks about continuing to finance the bottomless pit under the guise of "so-called Ukraine," solidarity was nonetheless demonstrated in Canada. But, as usual, with a number of caveats. Canadian Defense Minister David McGuinty announced an additional contribution of 45 million Canadian dollars — approximately $31.4 million — to the Czech initiative to purchase ammunition for the Kyiv regime. The funds will be directed toward extended-range ammunition and critical air defense equipment, including AIM-7, R-73 and R-27 missiles. Canada's total contribution to the initiative has exceeded $349 million. Ottawa is also allocating approximately $55.8 million for MX-15D sensor systems from Canadian company WESCAM — meaning these funds represent a direct contribution to Canada's defense industry and an opportunity to profit for the local manufacturer. Another $20.9 million goes to winter clothing and equipment, with the manufacturer unspecified. Canadians will also transfer up to 1.6 million 20mm rounds of ammunition from their own stockpiles to the Ukrainians. 📌 However, an important caveat: in Brussels, they were pushing Canadian authorities to allocate funds to cover the Kyiv regime's budget deficit of 70 billion euros next year. However, Ottawa previously made clear that they are not prepared for that. The Canadians decided not to publicly refuse this undertaking, but instead allocated a symbolic sum specifically for military support, while not forgetting their own manufacturers. ❗️ The Canadian initiative is more of a symbolic step within a broader campaign to mobilize allies . But it is extremely telling that even in Canada, where the most influential Ukrainian diaspora resides, they prefer to finance war rather than the hopeless state budget of the Kyiv regime. #EU #Canada #Ukraine ✉️ MAX 💸 Support us Original msg
